title: Resultative Sublatives of Texture, Consistency, and Surface Finish

sections.title: Transforming Substances: Liquid Reduction and Solid Texture
sections.content: Advanced culinary writing relies on exact resultative adjectives affixed with -ra/-re to indicate physical transformations in cooking. In sauce preparation, reduction is marked as 'sűrűre forral' (boils thick) or 'fényesre redukál' (reduces glossy). In baking and roasting, crust formation is marked as 'ropogósra süt' (bakes crispy) or 'keményre karamellizál' (caramelizes hard).

sections.title: Verbs of Culinary Technique Combined with -ra/-re
sections.content: Key technical pairs include: 'habosra ver' (beats until frothy), 'simára kever' (stirs until smooth), 'puhára párol' (braises until tender), and 'aranybarnára pirít' (browns golden). The sublative ending guarantees that the noun or adjective represents an achieved terminal milestone resulting from the cook's action.

sections.title: Texture and Consistency Resultatives
rows: A cukrász keményre karamellizálta a cukrot.
The confectioner caramelized the sugar hard.
A mártást selymesre és simára keverték.
The sauce was stirred silky and smooth.
A levest sűrűre beforralták az ünnepi asztalra.
The soup was boiled down thick for the festive table.

items.spanish: A szakács addig forralta a mártást, amíg sűrűre és selymesre nem sűrűsödött.
items.english: The chef boiled the sauce until it thickened thick and silky.

items.spanish: A torta tetejét ropogósra karamellizált cukorlappal vonták be.
items.english: The top of the cake was coated with a crispy caramelized sugar sheet.

items.spanish: A tejszínt keményre verték a desszert díszítéséhez.
items.english: The cream was whipped stiff/hard for decorating the dessert.

sections.title: B2 Usage Notice
sections.content: Do not confuse the resultative sublative (-ra/-re) with adverbs answering 'hogyan?'. If the recipe instructs: 'keverd simára' (stir it until it becomes smooth), 'simára' is a resultative sublative denoting the target condition.
